tagline: Eighty-eight miles of trout streams, dolomite bluffs and buggy traffic.
intro: Minnesota Highway 16 follows the Root River valley for 88 miles between La Crescent and Dexter, under wooded dolomite bluffs and past pasture and fields. Trout streams run down out of the hills, and an Amish buggy on the country roads is an ordinary part of the traffic.
The valley towns come along in turn, Houston and Rushford and Preston among them, and between Spring Valley and Preston a state park holds a restored 1899 village and the state's longest cave.

moments.title: Lanesboro
moments.text: A Fillmore County town of about 700 on the South Branch of the Root River, with a waterfall dam across from Sylvan Park.

moments.title: Historic Forestville
moments.text: A village restored to its 1899 appearance, where costumed interpreters show daily life; it stands inside Forestville/Mystery Cave State Park.

moments.title: Mystery Cave
moments.text: Minnesota's longest cave, in the same state park, open for naturalist-guided tours.
